payload.title: Paros Wedding Venues and How to Get Married There
payload.excerpt: Paros wedding venues sit in three parts of the island: Naoussa and the bays of the north coast, Parikia and the hills above its gulf in the west, and Golden Beach on the east coast.
key_takeaways: Monastiri and The Secret View have no guest rooms, so guests stay in nearby hotels, and The Secret View says it is happy to organise shuttles.
Only two of the eight venues here publish wedding capacities: Petra Farm (a chapel for 120 and an event space for 150) and The Secret View (110 for a terrace ceremony, 120 for dinner).
Six of the eight venues have a chapel on site, but only The Secret View names a ceremony type (symbolic), so ask the others which ceremonies their chapel takes before you plan around one.
The Municipality of Paros runs a civil marriages section, so check its steps, documents and any fees with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens well before you book.

faq.q: Which part of Paros suits a wedding?
faq.a: It depends on your guest list and the setting you want. Naoussa and the north has the most venues here, including a five-star hotel and a farm estate above Kolymbithres bay. Parikia and the west looks over the port town and its gulf, and Golden Beach on the east coast offers a beachfront hotel and an estate in the hills.

faq.q: Can we book a venue or villa on Paros for exclusive use?
faq.a: Yes, at some. Villa Mira Paros offers the whole property for your day, and The Secret View gives couples full access to every area for 24 hours. The other venues here do not publish exclusive use, so ask each one directly.

faq.q: Can Australians legally marry on Paros?
faq.a: Plan the legal steps before the venue. As at November 2026, you may need a Certificate of No Impediment, so ask the Greek embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia and whether it needs an apostille, and a marriage valid in Greece that would also be valid under Australian law is in most cases recognised in Australia. Check the current requirements with the Municipality of Paros and the Australian Embassy in Athens.

faq.q: Can we have a civil ceremony at the Paros town hall?
faq.a: The Municipality of Paros has a Civil Marriages section within its Registry Office. Ask the municipality for the steps that apply to foreign couples, and the Australian Embassy in Athens about your documents and any fees, before you set a date.

faq.q: How do guests get to Paros?
faq.a: Guests can fly from Athens, about 45 minutes, into Paros Airport, 9 km southwest of Parikia. Others take the ferry from Piraeus or Rafina to Parikia, which runs all year. Ferries can be delayed by strong winds, so guests should reconfirm departures.

faq.q: When should we marry on Paros?
faq.a: At the nearest official weather station, on Naxos, July and August are the warmest and driest months: mean maximums run from about 22°C in May and October to 27.1°C in July, and rain days are fewest from June to August. As at November 2026, heatwaves are frequent in Greece over summer and wildfires occur from June to September, so a summer date needs shade and a covered fallback.
